setting: A fictional Monday morning in an office kitchen.

presentation.situation: {{name}} is making coffee on Monday morning. {{name}} {{weekend}}. Make natural small talk, ask follow-up questions, and move smoothly to work: you need {{ask}}.
presentation.opening: Morning! Coffee? How was your weekend?

brief.you_are: You are chatting with a coworker before work starts.
brief.situation: {{name}} is making coffee on Monday morning. {{name}} {{weekend}}. Make natural small talk, ask follow-up questions, and move smoothly to work: you need {{ask}}.
brief.task: Open naturally, ask a follow-up question, and then move smoothly to the work topic.
brief.done_looks_like: The chat felt natural, you showed interest, and you got to your work question.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are chatting with a coworker before work starts.
goals: Open naturally, ask a follow-up question, and then move smoothly to the work topic.

card.want: A friendly start to the day, and to get to the desk on time.
card.speech: Casual, natural workplace English with contractions.
tactics: Share a little, and wait to be asked more
Answer a work question once it comes

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

objectives.evidence: The learner responds or opens naturally.
alternatives: Morning! It was good, thanks. How was yours?

objectives.evidence: The learner asks a real follow-up question.
alternatives: Oh nice, where did you go?

objectives.evidence: The learner makes a natural transition to work.
alternatives: By the way, about the report, could you...?

signals: \b(?:how was|how is|did you|good morning|morning|how about you)\b
beats.orient: We're just chatting in the kitchen. Tell me something about your weekend, and ask about mine.

signals: \b(?:where did|who did|what did|how did|did you|was it|what was)\b
opportunity: It was a really nice change.
beats.orient: I told you about my weekend. Ask me something more about it. You can say: Oh, where did you go?
fallback: It was a really nice change.

signals: \b(?:by the way|speaking of|about the|shall we discuss|project|work)\b
opportunity: Anyway, I should probably get to my desk.
Right, big week ahead. Anything I can do for you?
beats.orient: Now move to your work question. Start with: By the way.
fallback: Right, big week ahead. Anything I can do for you?
Anyway, I should probably get to my desk.

closing_line: No problem, I will sort that out. Have a good one!

o1.good: Answering briefly, and returning the question.
common_mistakes: A long answer, or just: Fine
o1.micro_lesson: Answer in a few words, then ask: How was yours?

o2.good: A follow-up shows that you were listening.
o2.micro_lesson: Pick one detail and ask about it.
o2.model: Oh nice, who did you go with?

o3.good: A small phrase makes the change of topic feel natural.
o3.micro_lesson: Say: By the way, or: Speaking of work.
o3.model: By the way, could you send me that file today?
